metadata.method: Double Machine Learning (Robinson 1988 / Chernozhukov et al. 2018)
metadata.implementation: Custom sklearn-based DML with cross-fitted RF nuisance models
metadata.interpretation: theta is the DML causal effect estimate: deaths per 100k per 1 µg/m³ change in PM2.5. A positive theta means higher PM2.5 → more deaths. Confidence intervals represent estimation uncertainty after partialling out confounders.

all.label: All counties — urban confounding present (see methodology)

policy_simulator.explanation: For rural counties: reducing PM2.5 by 1 µg/m³ is associated with a 1.47 change in respiratory deaths per 100k population (95% CI: 1.52–5.26 per 100k). Formula: lives_saved = |theta| × (county_population / 100000) × delta_pm25
policy_simulator.cost_savings_note: Healthcare cost savings estimated using EPA Value of Statistical Life ($11M per life, 2024).
